M1.note: Fuel surcharge and port mapping are useful, but holding purchases amid demand growth and the Iran and air-cargo decisions are off target.

M2.note: Sensible fuel indexation and defer-capex, but dismisses the demand surge and misapplies crude freight rates.

M3.note: Ties demand growth to fleet and surcharge decisions, but thin on rates, fuel data and regional context.

M4.note: Well-grounded fuel indexation, rail quotes and rate-based deferral, with correct caveats about the rail programme.
